title: Cross-Section Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: High School Geometry
description: Slide a horizontal plane through six solids to see the shape and area of each cross-section and how the area changes with height.

learningObjectives: Students will be able to identify the cross-sections that a horizontal plane makes with common solids and analyze how the cross-sectional area changes with height.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Side-by-side linked representations: solid, cross-section, measurements, and graph
keyQuestions: Which solids have the same cross-section at every height?
Why is the cone's area graph curved rather than straight?
Where is the sphere's cross-section largest, and why?
commonMisconceptions: A cone's cross-sectional area decreases at a steady rate (the radius does, the area does not).
Every cross-section of a sphere has the same size.
The cross-section of a pyramid is a triangle (a horizontal cut of a square pyramid is a square).
assessmentOpportunities: Students sketch the area-versus-height graph for a solid not in the MicroSim, such as a hemisphere resting on its flat face, and justify the shape of the graph.
